leftEvidence.title: Rabbah falls and its people are put to labor

points.label: Action and response
points.left: Joab captures the royal city and summons David, who takes the crown, removes spoil, brings out the inhabitants, and puts them to labor before returning to Jerusalem.
points.right: Amnon schemes through Jonadab, violates Tamar despite her speech, drives her away, and leaves her desolate in Absalom’s house; David is angry and Absalom remains silent toward Amnon.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: The source places the war left in chapter 11 closes with conquest and coerced labor inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
points.right: The source places violence enters David’s household while the king’s anger produces no narrated action inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.

payload.posture: 2 Samuel 12:26–31 and 2 Samuel 13:1–22 are distinct approved David Scenes in the authored “Taking, Rebuke, and House Fracture” movement; holding them together exposes what continues and what changes without collapsing their sources.

rightEvidence.title: Tamar names the wrong while David hears

payload.tension: 2 Samuel 12:26–31 foregrounds the war left in chapter 11 closes with conquest and coerced labor; 2 Samuel 13:1–22 foregrounds violence enters David’s household while the king’s anger produces no narrated action. Their sequence does not by itself explain every change between them.
